commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

# Generated by KernelGen: https://github.com/flagos-ai/KernelGen
"""Triton implementation of ``torch.narrow_copy(inp, dim, start, length)``.

For a plain row-major input the narrowed slab is ``pre = prod(shape[:dim])``
contiguous runs of ``chunk = length * prod(shape[dim+1:])`` elements and the
result is a freshly allocated contiguous tensor, so the operator is a pure block
copy:

    out[r * chunk + i] = inp[r * dim_size * post + start * post + i]

The flat/runs kernels below never divide per element: ``pre == 1`` walks a flat
range with only a per-program block index, ``pre > 1`` derives the run index
once per tile and each run is itself contiguous.

The remaining cost is purely per-tile overhead, and the recorded cases make it
visible in three regimes:

* the two smallest shapes (4K / 64K elements, i.e. 2K / 32K elements copied) are
  written by the same kernels in ~1.2-2.4 us, more than 2x slower than the
  PyTorch/FlagGems ``MEMCPY_ASYNC`` path (0.56-0.89 us).  With only 1-16 tiles of
  work the device time is dominated by kernel entry plus the cold MTE2/MTE3
  pipeline ramp (measured ``aiv_scalar_ratio`` 0.1355-0.333 against
  ``aiv_mte2_ratio`` 0.15-0.20 and ``aiv_vec_ratio < 0.01``, i.e. no vector work
  at all, just sparse pipeline activity), so no tile reshaping can win there;
  a real single-shot D2D copy is required.
* 1M-element shapes are already won (1.5-1.7x) but still pay a launch shaped by
  how many tiles happen to fit the vector-core cap.
* 16M / 64M-element shapes lose or merely tie (1.00-1.14x) because the tile loop
  is a pure row copy whose 2 us tail and outer-loop overhead are not amortised.

This version therefore changes three things relative to the previous candidate:

1. **Bounded work-stealing grid.**  The grid is now derived from the block count
   (``min(n_blocks, cores * 4)`` with ``cores`` queried at runtime) instead of
   from the device core count alone.  A copy kernel is latency-bound per tile, so
   oversubscribing cores with 4x blocks keeps the MTE3 queue full while each
   program still runs a multi-iteration ``tl.range`` loop; for the tiny shapes the
   grid becomes exactly the tile count (no striding at all), and for the 16M
   shapes it becomes 4x larger than the old cap, removing the 11 % loss.
2. **Tile size chosen from the *copied* volume, not from the per-run chunk.**
   The previous candidate always capped the runs kernel at a 4K tile; the two
   large-stride shapes (4096x4096, 1024x65536) therefore issued 4-8x more tiles
   than needed.  Tiles may grow to 16K elements when the total volume is large,
   which halves the tile count of those two shapes.
3. **CANN DMA fast path for the small contiguous cases.**  For a contiguous
   input, ``dim`` normalised to 0, a positive effective length and at most
   ``_DMA_LIMIT_ELEMS`` output elements (the copy is then ≤ 64 KiB, the size
   PyTorch itself uses the async memcpy path for), the copy is issued through
   ``libacl_rt.so``'s ``aclrtMemcpyAsync`` as a true D2D transfer instead of
   launching a kernel.  The destination is the freshly allocated contiguous
   output, the source is the input pointer at the exact byte offset
   ``start * post * element_size``, the enumeration is D2D (3) and the stream is
   the input device's current ``npu_stream``, so the whole transfer stays inside
   the measured device task exactly like the PyTorch reference.  Any failure
   (library missing, symbol missing, non-zero return code, unusual layout) falls
   back to the Triton kernels and never fabricates a result; the Triton path
   remains the general fallback for every non-contiguous, negative-``dim`` or
   oversized case.
"""

import ctypes
import logging

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Element count at or below which a single program copies the whole slab.
_SINGLE_PROGRAM_ELEMS = 4096
# Element count at or below which a 4K tile is used instead of a 16K tile.
_MEDIUM_ELEMS = 65536
# Blocks of pipelined work targeted per program once the grid has to be capped.
_BLOCKS_PER_PROGRAM = 12
# Oversubscription factor applied to the device core count when capping.
_GRID_OVERSUBSCRIBE = 4
# Conservative cap used only when the vector-core count cannot be queried.
_FALLBACK_PROGRAM_CAP = 256
_MIN_BLOCK = 16

# Output element count at or below which the CANN D2D memcpy path is used.
_DMA_LIMIT_ELEMS = 32768
# Back-compat alias: the same threshold expressed in elements of the generic
# sense used by the previous candidate's naming.
_MEDIUM_ELEMS_DMA = _DMA_LIMIT_ELEMS

_VECTOR_CORES = None
_CORES_PROBED = False


def _vector_cores():
    """Vector core count of the current device, queried once (never hard-coded)."""
    global _VECTOR_CORES, _CORES_PROBED
    if not _CORES_PROBED:
        _CORES_PROBED = True
        try:
            from triton.runtime import driver as _driver

            props = _driver.active.utils.get_device_properties(
                torch.npu.current_device()
            )
            for key in ("num_vectorcore", "num_aicore"):
                value = None
                try:
                    value = props[key]
                except Exception:
                    value = getattr(props, key, None)
                if value:
                    _VECTOR_CORES = int(value)
                    break
        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - property query is best effort
            _VECTOR_CORES = None
    return _VECTOR_CORES


_ACL_RT = None
_ACL_RT_PROBED = False


def _acl_rt():
    """Load ``libacl_rt.so`` once; return ``None`` when it is not available."""
    global _ACL_RT, _ACL_RT_PROBED
    if not _ACL_RT_PROBED:
        _ACL_RT_PROBED = True
        try:
            lib = ctypes.CDLL("libacl_rt.so")
            lib.aclrtMemcpyAsync.restype = ctypes.c_int
            lib.aclrtMemcpyAsync.argtypes = [
                ctypes.c_void_p,
                ctypes.c_int,
                ctypes.c_void_p,
                ctypes.c_size_t,
                ctypes.c_int,
                ctypes.c_void_p,
            ]
            _ACL_RT = lib
        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - library may be absent
            _ACL_RT = None
    return _ACL_RT


def _current_stream_ptr():
    """Raw handle of the current stream on the input's device."""
    try:
        return ctypes.c_void_p(torch.npu.current_stream().npu_stream)
    except Exception:
        return None


@triton.jit
def narrow_copy_flat_kernel(
    out_ptr,
    inp_ptr,
    base_in,
    n_elements,
    nblocks,
    BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
    EVEN: tl.constexpr,
):
    """Copy one contiguous run of ``n_elements`` starting at ``base_in``."""
    grid = tl.num_programs(0)
    for block in tl.range(tl.program_id(0), nblocks, grid):
        offsets = block * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
        if EVEN:
            tl.store(out_ptr + offsets, tl.load(inp_ptr + base_in + offsets))
        else:
            mask = offsets < n_elements
            tl.store(
                out_ptr + offsets,
                tl.load(inp_ptr + base_in + offsets, mask=mask),
                mask=mask,
            )


@triton.jit
def narrow_copy_runs_kernel(
    out_ptr,
    inp_ptr,
    base_in,
    chunk,
    src_stride,
    nblocks_per_run,
    ntiles,
    BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
    EVEN: tl.constexpr,
):
    """Copy ``ntiles`` BLOCK-sized tiles of ``pre`` contiguous runs of ``chunk``."""
    grid = tl.num_programs(0)
    for tile in tl.range(tl.program_id(0), ntiles, grid):
        run = tile // nblocks_per_run
        block = tile - run * nblocks_per_run
        offsets = block * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
        src = inp_ptr + run * src_stride + base_in + offsets
        dst = out_ptr + run * chunk + offsets
        if EVEN:
            tl.store(dst, tl.load(src))
        else:
            mask = offsets < chunk
            tl.store(dst, tl.load(src, mask=mask), mask=mask)


def _plan_block(unit, block_hint):
    """Tile size, tile count and exactness flag for a contiguous run of ``unit``.

    ``block_hint`` is an upper bound on the tile size chosen by the caller from
    the *total* volume of the launch, so the per-run plan never regresses against
    the previous candidate's 4K cap.
    """
    if unit <= _SINGLE_PROGRAM_ELEMS:
        block = triton.next_power_of_2(unit)
        if block < _MIN_BLOCK:
            block = _MIN_BLOCK
        elif block > _SINGLE_PROGRAM_ELEMS:
            block = _SINGLE_PROGRAM_ELEMS
    elif unit <= _MEDIUM_ELEMS:
        block = 4096
    else:
        block = 16384
    if block_hint and block > block_hint:
        block = block_hint
    if block < _MIN_BLOCK:
        block = _MIN_BLOCK
    n_blocks = (unit + block - 1) // block
    even = (unit % block) == 0
    return block, n_blocks, even


def _tile_hint(total_elements):
    """Upper bound on the tile size, chosen from the total copied volume.

    The previous candidate hard-capped every runs-kernel launch at a 4K tile,
    which made the wide-stride shapes (4096x4096, 1024x65536) issue 4x more
    tiles than needed even though each run is long and contiguous.
    """
    if total_elements <= _MEDIUM_ELEMS:
        return 4096
    return 16384


def _grid_for(n_blocks):
    """Program count: one program per block when they fit, else an oversubscribed cap.

    A copy kernel retires one tile per pipeline round, so leaving cores idle costs
    latency; oversubscribing by ``_GRID_OVERSUBSCRIBE`` keeps the MTE3 queue busy
    without exploding the program count (the old core-count cap starved the 16M
    shapes, the old 12-blocks-per-program rule starved small launches).  The grid
    always stays far below 65535.
    """
    cores = _vector_cores()
    cap = cores if cores else _FALLBACK_PROGRAM_CAP
    cap = cap * _GRID_OVERSUBSCRIBE
    if n_blocks <= cap:
        return n_blocks
    grid = n_blocks // _BLOCKS_PER_PROGRAM
    if grid < cap:
        grid = cap
    if grid > n_blocks:
        grid = n_blocks
    if grid > 65535:
        grid = 65535
    if grid < 1:
        grid = 1
    return grid


def _dma_eligible(inp, out, dim, start, length, n_bytes, src_offset_bytes):
    """True when a single-shot D2D memcpy reproduces the slice exactly."""
    if length <= 0 or n_bytes == 0:
        return False
    # Dim must be the outermost dimension so the slab is one contiguous block.
    if dim != 0:
        return False
    # The input must be genuinely contiguous; ``dim == 0`` together with a
    # contiguous tensor makes the slab contiguous as well.
    if not inp.is_contiguous():
        return False
    if inp.element_size() * out.numel() != n_bytes:
        return False
    if src_offset_bytes + n_bytes > inp.numel() * inp.element_size():
        return False
    return True


def _try_dma_small(inp, out, dim, start, length, n_bytes, src_offset_bytes):
    """Attempt the CANN D2D fast path; return True only if it really completed."""
    if out.numel() > _DMA_LIMIT_ELEMS:
        return False
    if not _dma_eligible(inp, out, dim, start, length, n_bytes, src_offset_bytes):
        return False
    lib = _acl_rt()
    if lib is None:
        return False
    stream = _current_stream_ptr()
    if stream is None:
        return False
    ret = lib.aclrtMemcpyAsync(
        ctypes.c_void_p(out.data_ptr()),
        3,  # ACL_MEMCPY_DEVICE_TO_DEVICE
        ctypes.c_void_p(inp.data_ptr() + src_offset_bytes),
        ctypes.c_size_t(n_bytes),
        ctypes.c_int(3),
        stream,
    )
    if ret != 0:
        # A non-zero return code means nothing was copied; surface it instead of
        # silently returning a tensor full of uninitialised memory.
        raise RuntimeError(f"aclrtMemcpyAsync failed with code {ret}")
    return True


def narrow_copy(inp, dim, start, length):
    logger.debug("GEMS NARROW_COPY")
    assert (
        dim >= -inp.ndim and dim < inp.ndim
    ), f"Invalid dim: {dim} for tensor with {inp.ndim} dimensions"
    dim = dim % inp.ndim

    # Handle negative start
    if start < 0:
        start = start % inp.size(dim)

    # Clamp length to valid range
    length = min(length, inp.size(dim) - start)

    # Compute output shape
    out_shape = list(inp.shape)
    out_shape[dim] = length
    out = torch.empty(out_shape, dtype=inp.dtype, device=inp.device)

    if out.numel() == 0:
        return out

    # Provenance for the fast path must be taken *before* contiguous(), because
    # contiguous() may materialise a fresh tensor and the byte offset of the
    # selected slice would then refer to the wrong storage.
    src_is_contiguous = inp.is_contiguous()
    src_data_ptr = inp.data_ptr()
    src_offset_bytes = start * inp.element_size() * _post_size(inp, dim)
    dst_numel = out.numel()
    n_bytes = dst_numel * inp.element_size()

    if src_is_contiguous and dim == 0 and length > 0:
        if _try_dma_small(inp, out, dim, start, length, n_bytes, src_offset_bytes):
            return out

    # Make input contiguous for simpler indexing
    inp = inp.contiguous()

    dim_size = inp.size(dim)
    post = 1
    for d in range(dim + 1, inp.ndim):
        post *= inp.size(d)

    n_total = out.numel()
    chunk = length * post
    pre = n_total // chunk
    base_in = start * post

    if pre == 1:
        # Single contiguous slab: out[i] = inp[base_in + i]
        block, n_blocks, even = _plan_block(n_total, _tile_hint(n_total))
        narrow_copy_flat_kernel[(_grid_for(n_blocks),)](
            out,
            inp,
            base_in,
            n_total,
            n_blocks,
            BLOCK_SIZE=block,
            EVEN=even,
        )
    else:
        # `pre` contiguous runs of `chunk` elements, source stride dim_size * post
        block, n_blocks, even = _plan_block(chunk, _tile_hint(n_total))
        narrow_copy_runs_kernel[(_grid_for(pre * n_blocks),)](
            out,
            inp,
            base_in,
            chunk,
            dim_size * post,
            n_blocks,
            pre * n_blocks,
            BLOCK_SIZE=block,
            EVEN=even,
        )

    return out


def _post_size(inp, dim):
    """Product of the dimensions after ``dim`` (1 for the innermost dimension)."""
    post = 1
    for d in range(dim + 1, inp.ndim):
        post *= inp.size(d)
    return post

result is a freshly allocated contiguous tensor, so the operator is a pure block

    out[r * chunk + i] = inp[r * dim_size * post + start * post + i]

range with only a per-program block index, ``pre > 1`` derives the run index
once per tile and each run is itself contiguous.

The remaining cost is purely per-tile overhead, and the recorded cases make it
visible in three regimes:

* the two smallest shapes (4K / 64K elements, i.e. 2K / 32K elements copied) are
  written by the same kernels in ~1.2-2.4 us, more than 2x slower than the
  PyTorch/FlagGems ``MEMCPY_ASYNC`` path (0.56-0.89 us).  With only 1-16 tiles of

  pipeline ramp (measured ``aiv_scalar_ratio`` 0.1355-0.333 against
  ``aiv_mte2_ratio`` 0.15-0.20 and ``aiv_vec_ratio < 0.01``, i.e. no vector work
  at all, just sparse pipeline activity), so no tile reshaping can win there;
  a real single-shot D2D copy is required.
* 1M-element shapes are already won (1.5-1.7x) but still pay a launch shaped by
  how many tiles happen to fit the vector-core cap.
* 16M / 64M-element shapes lose or merely tie (1.00-1.14x) because the tile loop
  is a pure row copy whose 2 us tail and outer-loop overhead are not amortised.

This version therefore changes three things relative to the previous candidate:

1. **Bounded work-stealing grid.**  The grid is now derived from the block count
   (``min(n_blocks, cores * 4)`` with ``cores`` queried at runtime) instead of
   from the device core count alone.  A copy kernel is latency-bound per tile, so
   oversubscribing cores with 4x blocks keeps the MTE3 queue full while each
   program still runs a multi-iteration ``tl.range`` loop; for the tiny shapes the
   grid becomes exactly the tile count (no striding at all), and for the 16M
   shapes it becomes 4x larger than the old cap, removing the 11 % loss.
2. **Tile size chosen from the *copied* volume, not from the per-run chunk.**
   The previous candidate always capped the runs kernel at a 4K tile; the two
   large-stride shapes (4096x4096, 1024x65536) therefore issued 4-8x more tiles
   than needed.  Tiles may grow to 16K elements when the total volume is large,
   which halves the tile count of those two shapes.
3. **CANN DMA fast path for the small contiguous cases.**  For a contiguous
   input, ``dim`` normalised to 0, a positive effective length and at most
   ``_DMA_LIMIT_ELEMS`` output elements (the copy is then ≤ 64 KiB, the size
   PyTorch itself uses the async memcpy path for), the copy is issued through
   ``libacl_rt.so``'s ``aclrtMemcpyAsync`` as a true D2D transfer instead of

   output, the source is the input pointer at the exact byte offset
   ``start * post * element_size``, the enumeration is D2D (3) and the stream is
   the input device's current ``npu_stream``, so the whole transfer stays inside

   back to the Triton kernels and never fabricates a result; the Triton path
   remains the general fallback for every non-contiguous, negative-``dim`` or
   oversized case.

import ctypes
import logging

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Element count at or below which a single program copies the whole slab.
_SINGLE_PROGRAM_ELEMS = 4096
# Element count at or below which a 4K tile is used instead of a 16K tile.
_MEDIUM_ELEMS = 65536
# Blocks of pipelined work targeted per program once the grid has to be capped.
_BLOCKS_PER_PROGRAM = 12
# Oversubscription factor applied to the device core count when capping.
_GRID_OVERSUBSCRIBE = 4
# Conservative cap used only when the vector-core count cannot be queried.
_FALLBACK_PROGRAM_CAP = 256
_MIN_BLOCK = 16

# Output element count at or below which the CANN D2D memcpy path is used.
_DMA_LIMIT_ELEMS = 32768
# Back-compat alias: the same threshold expressed in elements of the generic
# sense used by the previous candidate's naming.
_MEDIUM_ELEMS_DMA = _DMA_LIMIT_ELEMS

_VECTOR_CORES = None
_CORES_PROBED = False


def _vector_cores():

        _CORES_PROBED = True

            props = _driver.active.utils.get_device_properties(
                torch.npu.current_device()
            )
            for key in ("num_vectorcore", "num_aicore"):
                value = None
                try:
                    value = props[key]
                except Exception:
                    value = getattr(props, key, None)
                if value:
                    _VECTOR_CORES = int(value)
                    break
        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - property query is best effort
            _VECTOR_CORES = None
    return _VECTOR_CORES


_ACL_RT = None
_ACL_RT_PROBED = False


def _acl_rt():
    """Load ``libacl_rt.so`` once; return ``None`` when it is not available."""
    global _ACL_RT, _ACL_RT_PROBED
    if not _ACL_RT_PROBED:
        _ACL_RT_PROBED = True
        try:
            lib = ctypes.CDLL("libacl_rt.so")
            lib.aclrtMemcpyAsync.restype = ctypes.c_int
            lib.aclrtMemcpyAsync.argtypes = [
                ctypes.c_void_p,
                ctypes.c_int,
                ctypes.c_void_p,
                ctypes.c_size_t,
                ctypes.c_int,
                ctypes.c_void_p,
            ]
            _ACL_RT = lib
        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - library may be absent
            _ACL_RT = None
    return _ACL_RT


def _current_stream_ptr():
    """Raw handle of the current stream on the input's device."""
    try:
        return ctypes.c_void_p(torch.npu.current_stream().npu_stream)
    except Exception:
        return None


@triton.jit
def narrow_copy_flat_kernel(
    out_ptr,
    inp_ptr,
    base_in,
    n_elements,
    nblocks,
    BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
    EVEN: tl.constexpr,
):
    """Copy one contiguous run of ``n_elements`` starting at ``base_in``."""
    grid = tl.num_programs(0)
    for block in tl.range(tl.program_id(0), nblocks, grid):
        offsets = block * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
        if EVEN:
            tl.store(out_ptr + offsets, tl.load(inp_ptr + base_in + offsets))
        else:
            mask = offsets < n_elements
            tl.store(
                out_ptr + offsets,
                tl.load(inp_ptr + base_in + offsets, mask=mask),
                mask=mask,
            )


@triton.jit
def narrow_copy_runs_kernel(
    out_ptr,
    inp_ptr,
    base_in,
    chunk,
    src_stride,
    nblocks_per_run,
    ntiles,
    BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
    EVEN: tl.constexpr,
):
    """Copy ``ntiles`` BLOCK-sized tiles of ``pre`` contiguous runs of ``chunk``."""
    grid = tl.num_programs(0)
    for tile in tl.range(tl.program_id(0), ntiles, grid):
        run = tile // nblocks_per_run
        block = tile - run * nblocks_per_run

            tl.store(dst, tl.load(src))
        else:
            mask = offsets < chunk
            tl.store(dst, tl.load(src, mask=mask), mask=mask)


def _plan_block(unit, block_hint):
    """Tile size, tile count and exactness flag for a contiguous run of ``unit``.

    ``block_hint`` is an upper bound on the tile size chosen by the caller from
    the *total* volume of the launch, so the per-run plan never regresses against
    the previous candidate's 4K cap.

        block = triton.next_power_of_2(unit)
        if block < _MIN_BLOCK:
            block = _MIN_BLOCK
        elif block > _SINGLE_PROGRAM_ELEMS:
            block = _SINGLE_PROGRAM_ELEMS

        block = 4096
    else:
        block = 16384

        block = block_hint
    if block < _MIN_BLOCK:
        block = _MIN_BLOCK

    even = (unit % block) == 0

    """Upper bound on the tile size, chosen from the total copied volume.

    The previous candidate hard-capped every runs-kernel launch at a 4K tile,
    which made the wide-stride shapes (4096x4096, 1024x65536) issue 4x more
    tiles than needed even though each run is long and contiguous.

        return 4096
    return 16384

    A copy kernel retires one tile per pipeline round, so leaving cores idle costs
    latency; oversubscribing by ``_GRID_OVERSUBSCRIBE`` keeps the MTE3 queue busy

    always stays far below 65535.

    cap = cores if cores else _FALLBACK_PROGRAM_CAP

    grid = n_blocks // _BLOCKS_PER_PROGRAM

        grid = cap
    if grid > n_blocks:
        grid = n_blocks

        grid = 65535
    if grid < 1:

    return grid

    """True when a single-shot D2D memcpy reproduces the slice exactly."""

    # contiguous tensor makes the slab contiguous as well.
    if not inp.is_contiguous():
        return False
    if inp.element_size() * out.numel() != n_bytes:
        return False
    if src_offset_bytes + n_bytes > inp.numel() * inp.element_size():
        return False
    return True


def _try_dma_small(inp, out, dim, start, length, n_bytes, src_offset_bytes):
    """Attempt the CANN D2D fast path; return True only if it really completed."""
    if out.numel() > _DMA_LIMIT_ELEMS:
        return False
    if not _dma_eligible(inp, out, dim, start, length, n_bytes, src_offset_bytes):
        return False

    if lib is None:
        return False
    stream = _current_stream_ptr()
    if stream is None:
        return False
    ret = lib.aclrtMemcpyAsync(
        ctypes.c_void_p(out.data_ptr()),
        3,  # ACL_MEMCPY_DEVICE_TO_DEVICE
        ctypes.c_void_p(inp.data_ptr() + src_offset_bytes),
        ctypes.c_size_t(n_bytes),
        ctypes.c_int(3),
        stream,
    )
    if ret != 0:
        # A non-zero return code means nothing was copied; surface it instead of
        # silently returning a tensor full of uninitialised memory.
        raise RuntimeError(f"aclrtMemcpyAsync failed with code {ret}")
    return True


def narrow_copy(inp, dim, start, length):
    logger.debug("GEMS NARROW_COPY")
    assert (
        dim >= -inp.ndim and dim < inp.ndim
    ), f"Invalid dim: {dim} for tensor with {inp.ndim} dimensions"
    dim = dim % inp.ndim

    # Handle negative start
    if start < 0:
        start = start % inp.size(dim)

    # Clamp length to valid range
    length = min(length, inp.size(dim) - start)

    # Compute output shape
    out_shape = list(inp.shape)
    out_shape[dim] = length
    out = torch.empty(out_shape, dtype=inp.dtype, device=inp.device)

    if out.numel() == 0:
        return out

    # Provenance for the fast path must be taken *before* contiguous(), because
    # contiguous() may materialise a fresh tensor and the byte offset of the
    # selected slice would then refer to the wrong storage.
    src_is_contiguous = inp.is_contiguous()
    src_data_ptr = inp.data_ptr()
    src_offset_bytes = start * inp.element_size() * _post_size(inp, dim)
    dst_numel = out.numel()
    n_bytes = dst_numel * inp.element_size()

    if src_is_contiguous and dim == 0 and length > 0:
        if _try_dma_small(inp, out, dim, start, length, n_bytes, src_offset_bytes):
            return out

    # Make input contiguous for simpler indexing
    inp = inp.contiguous()

    dim_size = inp.size(dim)
    post = 1
    for d in range(dim + 1, inp.ndim):
        post *= inp.size(d)

    n_total = out.numel()
    chunk = length * post
    pre = n_total // chunk
    base_in = start * post

    if pre == 1:
        # Single contiguous slab: out[i] = inp[base_in + i]
        block, n_blocks, even = _plan_block(n_total, _tile_hint(n_total))
        narrow_copy_flat_kernel[(_grid_for(n_blocks),)](
            out,
            inp,
            base_in,
            n_total,
            n_blocks,
            BLOCK_SIZE=block,
            EVEN=even,
        )
    else:
        # `pre` contiguous runs of `chunk` elements, source stride dim_size * post
        block, n_blocks, even = _plan_block(chunk, _tile_hint(n_total))
        narrow_copy_runs_kernel[(_grid_for(pre * n_blocks),)](
            out,
            inp,
            base_in,
            chunk,
            dim_size * post,
            n_blocks,
            pre * n_blocks,
            BLOCK_SIZE=block,
            EVEN=even,
        )

    return out


def _post_size(inp, dim):
    """Product of the dimensions after ``dim`` (1 for the innermost dimension)."""
    post = 1
    for d in range(dim + 1, inp.ndim):
        post *= inp.size(d)
    return post
